title: ASTU 1st Round Model Exit Exam
source: ASTU Software Engineering — 1st Round Model Exit Examination (2hr, 100 MCQs)

focusGuide.C++: Headers, pointers, arrays, recursion traces, file I/O, and scope rules.
focusGuide.Data Structures: Sorting stability, heaps, graphs, Big-O, and stack-based iteration.
focusGuide.Java / OOP: Encapsulation, aggregation, message passing, and Swing/BorderLayout behavior.
focusGuide.Web Development: HTML/CSS/JS, MVC, PWA, SOA, accessibility, and web security threats.
focusGuide.Android: Activities, resources, Profiler, layout_weight, sandboxing, and user consent.
focusGuide.Database: Three-schema architecture, EER, weak entities, conceptual/logical design, relations.
focusGuide.Operating Systems: Deadlock, fork(), microkernel vs hybrid, semaphores, and file metadata.
focusGuide.Software Engineering: Waterfall, architecture, design strategy, state machines, and quality metrics.
focusGuide.Software Engineering (Requirements): RE purpose, scope, emergent properties, ambiguity, and scope creep.
focusGuide.Software Architecture: High-level structure, styles, availability, blackboard, and Strategy pattern.
focusGuide.Project Management: Triple constraint/CCB, risk vs incident, scope, float, and integration testing.
focusGuide.Software Testing: Testing goals, automation, model-based testing, re-testing, and state transitions.
focusGuide.Software Maintenance: Code smells, technical debt, regression testing, and servicing-stage changes.
focusGuide.Networking: OSI layers, subnetting, routers, HTTPS, UDP, and repeaters.
focusGuide.Security: SQL injection, honeypots, IDS features, hash integrity, and business continuity.
focusGuide.AI / ML: Rule-based limits, Turing Test, linear separability, regression, accuracy, and search.

questions.text: Why is "App Sandboxing" considered a fundamental security feature in mobile OS?

options.text: It allows apps to share all data by default to improve speed
It ensures that each app runs in its own process with limited access to other apps' data
It creates a backup of the app in the cloud
It prevents the user from uninstalling system apps

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): It ensures that each app runs in its own process with limited access to other apps' data

questions.text: How does a professional mobile developer ethically handle "User Consent" for location tracking?

options.text: Request consent clearly at the moment the feature is needed and explain why it is used
Hide the consent in a long "Terms and Conditions" document
Track the location in the background and notify the user after one month
Assume consent is given if the user installs the app

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): Request consent clearly at the moment the feature is needed and explain why it is used

questions.text: What is the goal of the three-schema database architecture?

options.text: To introduce a decentralized data handling method.
To separate the user applications from the physical database.
To disallow concurrent data access for security reasons
To avoid insertion and deletion anomalies on the database

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): To separate the user applications from the physical database.

questions.text: What is the main reason to use Extended Entity Relation Model (EER)?

options.text: Some attributes may not be useful in superclass entity but applicable to subclass
Effectively map many to many relationships between subclasses and superclass
To represent the entity type or relationship type that has a multivalued attribute
Effectively maps the existence of weak entity with the owner entity type

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Effectively maps the existence of weak entity with the owner entity type

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true regrading a weak entity type?

options.text: A weak entity has a partial participation constraint with respect to its identifying relationship
Weak Entity does not have their own key attributes to identified from database
A weak entity type has a partial key to be identified and ensure database consistency
Weak entity type may have more than one identifying entity type in a relationship

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): A weak entity has a partial participation constraint with respect to its identifying relationship

questions.text: During database design, the team models real-world entities and their relationships. Why is a conceptual model important?

options.text: Conceptual modeling is helpful to enforces ACID rules.
Conceptual modeling defines physical storage to improve query speed
Conceptual modeling provides an abstract view of entities and relationships.

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Conceptual modeling provides an abstract view of entities and relationships.

questions.text: In database design, logical model mainly focuses on

options.text: Integration and sharing of data among multiple tables with specific DBMS software
Mapping of the high-level conceptual model into the implementation data model
Mapping subclass and supper class relationship in EER model
Creating macro level representation of real-world concept and entities

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Mapping of the high-level conceptual model into the implementation data model

questions.text: Which of the following is not characteristics of a relational?

options.text: The order of the rows is immaterial
All values in a column hold the same data type
Each column should have a unique name
Ordering of the columns name is important

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Ordering of the columns name is important

questions.text: Which strategy should the Project Manager use to address this change while maintaining the "Triple Constraint"?

options.text: Use the Change Control Board (CCB) to evaluate the impact on time and cost before approval.
Defer the feature to the Maintenance phase as "Perfective Maintenance."
Reduce the testing phase to accommodate the new development time.

questions.text: What is the difference between a "Risk" and an "Incident?"

questions.text: Which testing level focuses on the interaction between integrated modules?

questions.text: Which of the following best describes software testing?

options.text: The process of executing a program to detect bugs
A technique used to ensure software meets specified requirements
A method for evaluating system performance

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): The process of executing a program to detect bugs

questions.text: Which scenario would best require automated testing?

questions.text: What is the main purpose of Confirmation Testing (Re-testing)?

options.text: To ensure that fixed defects do not reappear after a change.
To ensure the change has successfully fixed the defect it was intended to fix.
To test unchanged parts of the system.
To test the overall performance of the system

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): To ensure the change has successfully fixed the defect it was intended to fix.

questions.text: A software tester is verifying the behavior of an ATM. The system allows a user to "Enter PIN," "View Balance," and "Withdraw Cash." If the PIN is entered incorrectly three times, the card is blocked. Which testing technique is most effective for visualizing and testing this sequential flow of events?

questions.text: Which of the following evaluations best describes the "God Object" code well?

options.text: A class that lacks sufficient documentation for maintenance.
A class that has grown too large and taken on too many responsibilities.
A class that is never instantiated during the system's execution.
A class that contains only private methods and no public interface.

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): A class that has grown too large and taken on too many responsibilities.

questions.text: Which evaluation explains why "Primitive Obsession" is considered a defect in long-term evolution?

options.text: Primitive types use more memory than complex objects in modern JVMs.
It makes the code incompatible with older versions of the compiler.
It hides the domain logic that should be encapsulated within small objects.
It prevents the use of standard math libraries.

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): It hides the domain logic that should be encapsulated within small objects.

questions.text: In maintenance estimation, what does "Technical Debt Interest" represent?

options.text: The recurring extra effort required to maintain poorly structured code.
The cost of the initial development of the feature.
The tax paid to software vendors for licenses.
The bonus paid to developers for working overtime.

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): The recurring extra effort required to maintain poorly structured code.

questions.text: Applying the principle of "Regression Testing" during maintenance is intended to:

options.text: Ensure that changes have not introduced new bugs into existing functionality.
Ensure that new features are working correctly.
Check if the code meets the latest coding style standards.
Validate the user interface's aesthetic appeal.

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): Ensure that changes have not introduced new bugs into existing functionality.

questions.text: When a system is in the "Servicing" stage of the evolution model, what kind of changes are typically made?

options.text: Migration to a completely new platform.
Total redesign of the user interface.
Only small patches and bug fixes.

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): Only small patches and bug fixes.
